source_refs.note: Topic 11.7.1 (Structure of Alkenes) with Figures 11.8 to 11.10 and the Interesting Information box, printed pages 256-257.

blocks.text: Ethene (C₂H₄) is the simplest alkene. Each carbon atom in ethene is sp² hybridized and forms three equivalent sp² hybrid orbitals which lie in the same plane. The unhybrid p-orbital lies perpendicular (90º) to the plane of hybrid orbitals shown in Figure 11.8.

These sp² orbitals are formed by mixing of the 2s orbital with two 2p orbitals leaving one unhybrid p orbital. In ethene, each carbon uses two sp² orbitals to form two C–H bonds each. The remaining sp² orbital on each carbon is used to form a carbon-carbon σ bond by linear overlap as in Figure 11.9.

The unhybrid p-orbitals of each carbon atom which are parallel to each other overlap laterally to form another carbon-carbon bond. This bond formed by the lateral overlap of p-orbitals is called a π bond.

blocks.title: Interesting Information!
blocks.text: Plants produce ethene as a natural ripening hormone. For efficiency harvesting and transportation to market, fruits and vegetables are often picked unripe and exposed to ethane so they could ripen in short time.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Ethene, not ethane, is the ripening hormone that unripe fruits and vegetables are exposed to, as the box's first sentence says.

blocks.caption: Figure 11.8: sp2 hybrid and unhybrid orbitals of C (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 11.8).

blocks.alt: Two carbons each with a vertical 2pz orbital (lobes above and below) joined by lines labelled pi-bond above and below. Between the carbons two sp2 lobes overlap end to end (sigma-bond). Each carbon has two more sp2 lobes overlapping the 1s orbitals of green H atoms (sigma-bonds).
blocks.caption: Figure 11.9: Bond formation of carbons in ethene (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 11.9).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 11.9 labels the hydrogen orbitals ‘IS’; they are 1s orbitals, as drawn above.
The two carbon atoms forming a double bond and the four atoms attached directly to them lie in the same plane. The remaining p-orbital on each carbon is used to form the π bond.
The sp² hybridization results in a trigonal planar arrangement around each carbon atom. The bond angles are approximately 120º, leading to a planar molecule as shown in Figure 11.10.

blocks.alt: Ethene: two C atoms joined by a double bond, with curved lines above and below the double bond for the pi electron cloud; each C carries two green H atoms; a red double-headed arc between the two H atoms on the left carbon is marked 120 degrees.
blocks.caption: Figure 11.10: Structure of ethene (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 11.10).
